title: Detecting neurobiological markers in treatment response to prolonged exposure therapy for PTSD: An RCT using functional near-infrared spectroscopy
author: Booysen, Zondo

steps.title: Recruit and screen participants
steps.instruction: Identify university students older than 18 years, register them via email list or QR‑code posters, and screen for PTSD using the PCL‑5 (score ≥ 28) and trauma duration of at least 3 months. Plan for N = 34 participants per arm (power = 0.8, target effect size d = 0.71).

steps.title: Obtain consent and baseline questionnaires
steps.instruction: Provide an online Google Form link containing the study information, consent form, demographic items, and baseline self‑report measures: PCL‑5, PHQ‑9, GAD‑7, and AUDIT.

steps.title: Schedule baseline fNIRS assessment
steps.instruction: Contact eligible participants to arrange an in‑person fNIRS session with the neuropsychology team (SZ and DB).

steps.title: Configure fNIRS hardware and optodes
steps.instruction: Set up the NIRxSport2 continuous‑wave device (NIRx, Berlin) with a pre‑frontal EasyCap headband. Attach eight LED emitters (sources) and seven photodiode detectors to create twenty‑two channels covering the prefrontal cortex. Place optodes according to the 10‑20 system and determine the most sensitive locations using the fOLD software, assigning each source/detector pair the corresponding MNI coordinates.

steps.title: Program facial‑expression paradigm
steps.instruction: Using PsychoPy, program a block design with thirty fearful faces (F), thirty neutral faces (N), and thirty blank‑screen (BS) trials presented in random order. Each stimulus is shown for 2 s, followed by a jittered inter‑trial interval of 4–9 s (blank screen). Include rest periods at the beginning and end of the run. Send event markers via Lab Streaming Layer to the Aurora Acquisition Software (NIRx).

steps.title: Run baseline fNIRS recording
steps.instruction: Have the participant sit comfortably, fit the headband, start the Aurora acquisition, and run the programmed facial‑expression paradigm while continuously recording oxygenated (HbO) and deoxygenated (deOxy) hemoglobin signals.

steps.title: Train treatment providers
steps.instruction: Deliver two separate 2‑day workshops on standard prolonged exposure (PE) and on prolonged exposure for primary care (PE‑PC), followed by a 4‑day workshop on supportive counselling (SC). Each training day lasts ≈ 7 h. After training, schedule weekly supervision consultations for each condition during the intervention phase.

steps.title: Randomise participants
steps.instruction: With the project statistician, randomise eligible participants 1:1 to either PE‑PC or SC using a computer‑generated sequence. Keep participants single‑blind to allocation.

steps.title: Deliver online interventions
steps.instruction: Conduct 4–8 weekly 30‑minute sessions via Zoom/Google Meet/MS Teams. For PE‑PC, each session includes assessment, psycho‑education, written trauma‑memory exposure, processing questions, and assignment of in‑vivo exposure. For SC, provide non‑directive, person‑centred counselling (empathy, non‑judgement, congruence).

steps.title: Record sessions and monitor fidelity
steps.instruction: Video‑ and audio‑record all therapy sessions. Have providers complete a fidelity self‑report after each session. An independent reviewer will assess at least 20 % of recordings for adherence to the protocol.

steps.title: Collect outcome measures at all time points
steps.instruction:
Administer the following at each scheduled assessment:
- T1 (pre‑intervention): PCL‑5, PHQ‑9, GAD‑7, AUDIT, and the baseline fNIRS paradigm.
- T2 (during intervention): PCL‑5 and PHQ‑9 before every session (self‑completed or with provider assistance).
- T3 (post‑intervention): repeat all T1 questionnaires, repeat fNIRS paradigm, and administer the Perceived Characteristics of Intervention Scale (PCIS).
- T4 (12‑week follow‑up) and T5 (24‑week follow‑up): repeat the T1 questionnaires.
All questionnaires are self‑report and collected online.

steps.title: Analyse fNIRS data
steps.instruction: Import raw HbO and deOxy signals into Satori fNIRS (NIRx) and preprocess (motion‑artifact correction). Convolve stimulus onset times for F, N, and BS blocks with the canonical hemodynamic response function to create regressors. Apply a General Linear Model separately for each participant’s HbO and deOxy data. Export beta estimates and conduct group‑level linear mixed‑effects models and t‑tests in JASP (v0.18) to compare conditions.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis of clinical outcomes
steps.instruction: Use an intention‑to‑treat mixed‑model ANOVA to test differences across the five assessment points (baseline, post‑intervention, 12‑week, 24‑week). Compute Hedges’ g effect sizes for baseline vs. post‑intervention and follow‑up (interpret 0.2 = small, 0.5 = medium, 0.8 = large).
